label: Jun 19, 2026
headline: US to revive domestic H-1B visa renewal pilot in December — ~20,000 slots, mostly for Indians
summary: Julie Stufft, Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Visa Services, confirmed the US will launch a domestic visa renewal pilot for certain H-1B holders starting December, allowing eligible workers already inside the US to renew without traveling abroad for a consular interview. The State Department will issue about 20,000 visas over the first three months, and Stufft said the 'vast majority' will go to Indian nationals — the largest skilled-worker group in the US — with plans to expand. She acknowledged India's 6-to-12-month interview wait times are 'not what we need,' and said the program will free up US missions in India to focus on first-time applicants. A Federal Register notice with eligibility rules and application steps is expected soon. The move, flagged in the recent India-US joint statement and welcomed by the diaspora, revives the domestic revalidation concept first piloted in early 2024.
source: US State Department (Julie Stufft) / The Indian Eye / EY

label: Jun 15, 2026
headline: US Embassy India opens thousands of student visa slots for July–August — more to come amid portal glitches
summary: The US Embassy in India announced via @USAndIndia that since the F/M/J student visa appointment portal opened on June 14, thousands of Indian students have secured interview slots for July and August, with thousands more appointments still available and additional batches to open in the coming weeks. The opening-day rush triggered technical glitches on the scheduling portal; the embassy urged applicants not to refresh their accounts too frequently to avoid being locked out, and said it is working to resolve the issues. This is the main release of student visa appointments ahead of the Fall 2026 intake, critical timing for the large cohort of Indian students joining US colleges.

label: Jun 12, 2026
headline: EB-5 investor visa cap exhausted for India — no new unreserved visas until October 2026
summary: The US State Department confirmed that all EB-5 unreserved immigrant visas for Indian nationals have been fully allocated for FY2026 as of June 5. US embassies and consulates will not issue any more EB-5 unreserved visas to Indians until the new fiscal year begins October 1, 2026. The EB-5 program lets foreign investors apply for permanent residency by investing in US businesses that create 10+ jobs. Set-aside categories (Rural, High Unemployment Area, Infrastructure) remain current for Indian applicants. This comes weeks after the EB-2 professional category also hit its India cap in May.
source: US State Department / June 2026 Visa Bulletin

label: Jun 10, 2026
headline: Modi to raise H-1B visa issue with Trump at G7 summit in France
summary: PM Modi is expected to hold bilateral talks with President Trump at the G7 summit in Evian-les-Bains, France (June 15–17), with H-1B visas, trade, and energy on the agenda. India is pushing back on recent visa restrictions that have rattled its tech workforce and outsourcing industry. The meeting follows Rubio's India visit last month and comes as both sides move toward a bilateral trade deal potentially closing by mid-July.

label: Jun 10, 2026
headline: Rep. Kennedy introduces PROTECT Act to codify $100K H-1B fee in law
summary: One day after Judge Sorokin struck down Trumps $100K H-1B fee as an unauthorized tax, Rep. Mike Kennedy (R-UT) introduced the PROTECT Act to codify the same fee at the congressional level — bypassing the constitutional objection by making it an explicit act of Congress. The bill requires H-1B employers to pay the greater of prevailing wages or $100K base. Even with the court victory, the legislative push means the fee fight is far from over for Indian tech workers.

label: Jun 9, 2026
headline: State Dept launches $750 "premium" B1/B2 visa service — interview within 10 days
summary: The State Department will offer a $750 add-on for B-1/B-2 visa applicants to schedule an interview within 10 business days — on top of the $185 base fee. The pilot runs July 1 through Dec 31 at select embassies/consulates (to be announced). Timed to ease FIFA World Cup 2026 visa backlogs. Critical for India where B1/B2 waits range from 5.5 months (Delhi/Chennai) to 7.5 months (Mumbai). Does NOT guarantee visa approval — only faster interview scheduling.
source: US State Department / AP / Bloomberg Law

label: Jun 8, 2026
headline: Federal judge strikes down Trump's $100,000 H-1B visa fee — rules it an unlawful tax
summary: U.S. District Judge Leo Sorokin in Boston vacated Trump's $100,000 H-1B visa fee in a lawsuit brought by 20 state attorneys general, ruling it an unauthorized tax Congress never approved. Prior fees were $2K–$5K; only 85 employers had paid the $100K since September. The White House is appealing, citing a conflicting ruling from a D.C. judge who upheld the fee. The fee's fate now hinges on the appeals courts — but for now, it is vacated in its entirety.
source: U.S. District Court / Reuters / USA TODAY

label: Jun 8, 2026
headline: DOJ launches largest denaturalization push in modern history — Indian H-1B fraud case among 17 stripped of citizenship
summary: The Department of Justice filed denaturalization actions in federal courts against 17 naturalized citizens, in what the Washington Examiner called the largest coordinated denaturalization campaign in modern US history. Among them is Neeraj Sharma, 50, an India-born owner of New Jersey IT staffing firm Magnavision LLC, who filed 11 fraudulent H-1B petitions with forged corporate letterhead and then concealed the fraud on his 2017 naturalization application. Acting AG Todd Blanche said the DOJ now maintains a 'zero-tolerance policy' for abuse of the naturalization process. Denaturalization, averaging just 11 cases/year from 1990-2017, is being sharply expanded — a direct warning to naturalized Indian citizens who obtained status through visa or immigration misrepresentation.
source: US Department of Justice / USA TODAY / Washington Examiner

label: Jun 6, 2026
headline: US busts India-linked H-1B fraud ring — 100,000+ fake degree certificates seized
summary: Federal authorities uncovered a major India-linked visa fraud operation, seizing over 100,000 fake degree certificates from institutions including Manav Bharti University. Degrees sold for as little as $1,400 were used to qualify for H-1B visas. ICE identified 10,000+ students linked to "highly suspect employers" through OPT. USCIS admitted it does not track degrees from flagged institutions — expect heightened credential scrutiny for Indian applicants.

label: Jun 4, 2026
headline: Bill introduced to end H-1B as green card pathway & eliminate OPT program
summary: Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX) introduced the "American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act of 2026" — would replace the H-1B lottery with wage-based selection, end H-1B as a route to permanent residency, eliminate the OPT program for foreign graduates, and require employers to prove no qualified Americans are available before hiring H-1B workers. Still a bill, not law, but signals escalating Congressional pressure on the program.

label: Jun 2, 2026
headline: USTravelDocs & CEAC hit by outages — scheduling and payments disrupted
summary: US visa processing websites including USTravelDocs.com and CEAC are experiencing significant technical issues, delaying interview bookings, fee payments, and document uploads. India is among the hardest-hit countries. State Dept working on fix, no timeline given. Applicants advised to retry after 24 hours.

label: Jun 2, 2026
headline: 200K+ H-1B applicants paid $100K each for 15-day processing — standard wait now 7.5 months
summary: DHS Secretary Mullin testified before Senate that of 286,000 H-1B applications in FY2026, over 200,000 paid $100,000 for expedited 15-day processing. Standard processing now takes 7.5 months. Senators pushing for exemptions for doctors and teachers in rural/underserved communities.

label: Jun 1, 2026
headline: US Embassy India warns: visa screening continues after issuance — violators face revocation & deportation
summary: @USAndIndia posted that screening does not stop once a visa is issued. Holders are continuously monitored for compliance with US laws and immigration rules — visas will be revoked and holders deported if found in violation. Part of broader enforcement posture alongside expanded social media vetting.

label: May 30, 2026
headline: DHS walks back Green Card return-home rule — now case-by-case
summary: After backlash to the May 23 directive, DHS clarifies most green card applicants will NOT be required to leave the US. Adjustment of status called 'extraordinary relief' but officers decide case-by-case — no blanket exit mandate.

label: May 27, 2026
headline: EB-2 India green card quota fully exhausted for FY2026
summary: All EB-2 immigrant visa numbers for India used up. Final Action Date retrogressed to Sep 2013. No new EB-2 green cards for Indians until FY2027 begins Oct 2026.

label: May 26, 2026
headline: Rubio freezes student visa appointments worldwide
summary: US State Department halts all new F-1 visa appointments. Indian fall enrollments already in freefall.

label: May 24, 2026
headline: Rubio launches "AppUS" — new America First visa scheduling tool
summary: Prioritises business professionals who strengthen US-India commercial ties. Announced during Rubio's first India visit as Secretary of State.

label: May 23, 2026
headline: Green Card applicants must return to home country to apply
summary: US government announces that those seeking a Green Card must now return to their home countries to file — a major shift affecting thousands of Indian applicants. (Update: DHS partially walked this back on May 30.)

label: May 12, 2026
headline: ICE launches nationwide crackdown on Day 1 CPT and OPT fraud
summary: ICE announced coordinated enforcement targeting schools, students, and employers involved in fraudulent CPT/OPT programs. Thousands of Indian professionals who used Day 1 CPT to maintain F-1 status between H-1B lottery attempts now face scrutiny — prior CPT use may affect pending H-1B petitions.

label: Sep 2025
headline: Interview waiver eliminated for work & student visas
summary: H-1B, H-4, L-1, F-1, J-1, O-1 applicants no longer qualify for interview waiver. All must attend in-person interviews.
